record.title: EU AI Office opens an EDIH catalogue pilot for deployment-ready European AI providers
record.summary: On 17 November 2026, the European Commission AI Office opened a call inviting European AI providers with mature, SME-deployable solutions to present them to the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs). The first edition is limited to up to 100 providers; the Commission plans to list selected solutions in an “EDIH Ready” catalogue on the AI-on-Demand Platform so EDIHs can connect them with small and medium-sized enterprises. The source establishes the call and its intended design, not provider selection, SME deployment, adoption or economic impact.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The European Commission AI Office published a call for expression of interest for European AI providers on 17 November 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The Commission says the first edition invites up to 100 European providers with mature, SME-ready AI solutions; selected solutions are planned for an “EDIH Ready” catalogue on the AI-on-Demand Platform, with EDIHs acting as intermediaries to SMEs.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The call page does not establish which providers will be selected, whether the catalogue will generate SME deployments, or any adoption, productivity or economic effect.

evidence_gaps.description: No selected-provider list, populated EDIH Ready catalogue or resulting SME deployments are reported at launch.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, an EU-level “EDIH Ready” catalogue and hub-mediated matching can reduce discovery friction between European AI suppliers and SME buyers, a material adoption channel. This is a first-edition pilot capped at 100 providers; selection, deployment and economic effects are not yet established.
limitations: This is a call announcement and planned catalogue, not evidence that any provider was selected, listed or deployed by an SME.
Eligibility is limited to European AI providers whose solutions are mature and ready for SME deployment; research projects, proofs of concept and MVPs are excluded.
The Commission gives the call publication date but no publication time, so the exact event age against a strict 36-hour window is unresolved.

technical.claimed_result: The Commission states the pilot will invite up to 100 providers and aims to bridge AI supply and SME demand.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official call page and eligibility/deadline were published; no implementation outcome is yet demonstrated.
technical.mechanism: The AI Office solicits provider submissions; the planned AI-on-Demand catalogue gives EDIHs a curated list for matching solutions to SME needs and may support later matchmaking or demonstrations.
technical.regime: European Commission pilot call for market-ready AI solution providers and SME matching through the EDIH network.
technical.strongest_baseline: The Commission describes the existing EDIH network as serving over 50,000 organisations; no comparable baseline for AI-provider discovery or SME adoption is given.

brief.title: EU AI Office opens an EDIH catalogue pilot for deployment-ready European AI providers
brief.why_it_matters: This is a concrete EU mechanism to connect AI supply with SME demand through a network of regional intermediaries, complementing general funding and strategy announcements with a provider-discovery route. The pilot is open through 17 December 2026 and targets solutions ready for deployment; whether it changes adoption remains to be measured.
